Use case: stylized-concept. National cultural heritage travel illustration in the visual style of Day of the Tentacle adventure-game backgrounds with strongly exaggerated wonky angular architecture, crooked perspective and thick dark plum ink contours, combined with sculpted cel-shaded 3D volume, soft cast shadows, ambient occlusion and visible layered depth. NOT a realistic photo. Clear foreground/middle/background separation for parallax shader presentation, atmospheric distant scenery, bold silhouettes and rich organized details. Use real recognizable landmarks from the specified country only, regionally accurate natural animals in separate appropriate habitats. No invented landmark combinations presented as a literal place: this is explicitly a national travel montage. Natural animals without clothes, anthropomorphism or silly expressions. No octopuses, tentacles, fantasy creatures, silly characters or people. No words, lettering, flags, logos, watermarks or national emblems. Represent listed authentic regional sites without inventing extra religious buildings. Final composition is a broad representative regional selection, never all districts or exhaustive heritage. Keep every primary landmark roof and all animal silhouettes fully inside frame, with margins. Country: Benin. Palette from supplied collection: #D1E395 #91D2CC #76B8E6 #91D69A, supported by muted natural stone, wood and vegetation colors with purple shadows. Natural animals in appropriate separate habitats: elephant in Pendjari, roan antelope. Local plants: oil palm, baobab. Small optional authentic craft/food detail: appliqué textiles. Cover panorama3:1 final1500x500. Clear broad region clusters from left to right, animal foreground near lower-right and plants lower-left; ample upper breathing room, mountains and sky far behind.

Benin earthen palace walls with reliefs, stilt village over water, Ouidah memorial arch, compact earthen Tata Somba homes. Natural elephant lower-right with entire tusks/trunk/body inside frame; antelope separate savanna. Oil palm lower-left. All heritage rooftops visible, wide3:1.
